sources.entry: configparser - (Python standard library) INI file parser.

summary.name: configparser
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module for reading and writing INI-style configuration files via the ConfigParser class.
use_cases: Reading application settings from an INI file
Letting end users customize a Python program via a config file
Converting config values to ints, floats, or booleans
Using variable interpolation between config values
Layering multiple config files with overrides
summary.what_it_does: The module provides the ConfigParser class, which reads and writes INI-style files made of sections, keys, and values. Values are always stored as strings, with getint(), getfloat(), and getboolean() helpers for conversion, plus fallback arguments for missing keys. A DEFAULT section supplies values to all other sections. Interpolation is available in two styles: BasicInterpolation using %(name)s and ExtendedInterpolation using ${section:option}. Parser behavior such as comment prefixes, delimiters, strictness, and custom converters can be customized at construction time.
notable: Part of the Python standard library, documented at docs.python.org
Supports DEFAULT section defaults and BasicInterpolation / ExtendedInterpolation
Mapping-protocol access like parser['section']['option'] with changes written back to the parser
Configurable comment prefixes, delimiters, strict duplicate checking, and custom converters
caveats: Does not interpret Windows Registry extended INI value-type prefixes
Untrusted INI input can consume considerable CPU and memory; limiting input size is recommended
Inline comments are disabled by default and can interfere with values
